# List (Stacked List) — Library Analysis

## Problem Statement

Stacked lists are one of the most common UI patterns in applications — user lists, activity feeds, notification panels, settings pages, search results. Yet AI code generators consistently produce poor implementations: non-responsive, hardcoded widths, broken text truncation, no semantic structure, and fragile avatar/text/action alignment that falls apart on mobile.

The core challenge is that a stacked list item has **variable anatomy** (avatar, icon, text block, metadata, badge, action button, menu) and each combination needs to stay aligned and responsive without custom CSS per variant.

### Reference: Tailwind UI Stacked Lists

Tailwind UI shows **15 variants** across three layout families:

| Family | Variants | Key Pattern |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| **Full-width** | Simple, with links, with avatars+actions, with badges+buttons, in card, two-column | `flex gap-4` row, `min-w-0` truncation, `divide-y` dividers |
| **Narrow** | Sticky headings, with actions, truncated, small avatars, with badges | Compact spacing, sidebar-friendly widths |
| **Responsive** | Avatar groups, inline links, constrained content | Adapts from stacked mobile to row desktop |

**Common HTML pattern across all variants:**
```html
<ul class="divide-y">
  <li class="flex items-center gap-x-4 px-4 py-4">
    <img class="size-12 rounded-full" />        <!-- leading visual -->
    <div class="min-w-0 flex-1">                 <!-- text block (truncates) -->
      <p class="font-semibold truncate">Name</p>
      <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 truncate">Description</p>
    </div>
    <div class="flex-none">                      <!-- trailing content -->
      <Badge />
      <Button />
    </div>
  </li>
</ul>
```

## Quick Comparison

| | MUI | Mantine | Ant Design | Chakra UI | shadcn/ui |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Props** | Rich: dense, disablePadding, subheader | Minimal: type, size, icon, spacing | Rich: bordered, loading, pagination, grid | Minimal: semantic only | Card-based composition |
| **Compound** | Deep: List > ListItem > ListItemAvatar + ListItemText + ListItemSecondaryAction + ListItemButton | Simple: List > List.Item (icon override) | Medium: List > List.Item > List.Item.Meta | Simple: List > ListItem | No List — uses Card compound |
| **Standout** | ListItemButton separates navigation from content; deep slot system | Per-item icon override; withPadding nesting | **List.Item.Meta** — avatar/title/description shorthand that auto-layouts | Semantic HTML focus | Composition-first, no dedicated List |

## Props Detail

### MUI — List & ListItem

| Prop | Type | Default |
|------|------|---------|
| dense | boolean | false |
| disablePadding | boolean | false |
| subheader | ReactNode | — |

**ListItem sub-components:**
- `ListItemAvatar` — wraps Avatar in correct sizing/alignment
- `ListItemIcon` — leading icon slot
- `ListItemText` — `primary` + `secondary` text with typography
- `ListItemButton` — makes entire row clickable
- `ListItemSecondaryAction` — absolutely positioned trailing action

```tsx
<List>
  <ListItem>
    <ListItemAvatar><Avatar src="..." /></ListItemAvatar>
    <ListItemText primary="Name" secondary="Description" />
    <ListItemSecondaryAction><IconButton /></ListItemSecondaryAction>
  </ListItem>
</List>
```

**Key insight:** MUI's deep sub-component tree means many imports for a single list item. The `ListItemSecondaryAction` using absolute positioning can cause overflow issues.

### Mantine — List

| Prop | Type | Default |
|------|------|---------|
| type | 'ordered' \| 'unordered' | 'unordered' |
| size | 'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl' | 'md' |
| icon | ReactNode | — |
| spacing | MantineSpacing | 0 |
| center | boolean | false |
| withPadding | boolean | false |
| listStyleType | string | — |

```tsx
<List spacing="xs" icon={<ThemeIcon><IconCheck /></ThemeIcon>}>
  <List.Item>Clone or download repository</List.Item>
  <List.Item>Install dependencies</List.Item>
</List>
```

**Key insight:** Mantine's List is really a **bullet list** component, not a stacked list. It handles ordered/unordered text lists with icons. The stacked-list pattern in Mantine is achieved through custom composition with Stack, Group, and other primitives.

### Ant Design — List

| Prop | Type | Default |
|------|------|---------|
| bordered | boolean | false |
| dataSource | any[] | — |
| grid | { gutter, column, xs, sm, md, lg, xl, xxl } | — |
| header | ReactNode | — |
| footer | ReactNode | — |
| itemLayout | 'horizontal' \| 'vertical' | 'horizontal' |
| loading | boolean \| SpinProps | false |
| loadMore | ReactNode | — |
| locale | { emptyText } | — |
| pagination | PaginationConfig \| false | false |
| renderItem | (item, index) => ReactNode | — |
| rowKey | string \| (item) => string | — |
| size | 'default' \| 'large' \| 'small' | 'default' |
| split | boolean | true |

**List.Item.Meta** — the key innovation:

| Prop | Type | Default |
|------|------|---------|
| avatar | ReactNode | — |
| title | ReactNode | — |
| description | ReactNode | — |

```tsx
<List
  dataSource={data}
  renderItem={item => (
    <List.Item actions={[<a>edit</a>, <a>more</a>]}>
      <List.Item.Meta
        avatar={<Avatar src={item.avatar} />}
        title={item.name}
        description={item.email}
      />
      <div>Content</div>
    </List.Item>
  )}
/>
```

**Key insight:** `List.Item.Meta` is brilliant — it takes `avatar`, `title`, `description` and auto-layouts them in the standard stacked-list pattern. Combined with `List.Item`'s `actions` prop (renders trailing action links), this covers 90% of stacked list use cases with minimal code. However, the `dataSource` + `renderItem` API feels like a data grid, not a component.

### Chakra UI — List

Simple semantic list (`<ul>`/`<ol>`) — not applicable for stacked lists. Chakra handles this through composition with HStack, VStack, Box.

### shadcn/ui

No dedicated List component. Uses Card compound components or raw composition. This is the "composition over components" approach — flexible but puts the layout burden on the consumer.

---

## The Core Design Problem

Looking across all libraries and the Tailwind UI examples, the stacked list item has a **three-zone layout** that must remain stable across all variants:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  [Leading]    [Content ··· truncates]  [Trailing]│
│   avatar       title                     badge   │
│   icon         description               button  │
│   checkbox     metadata                  menu    │
│                                          time    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**What makes this hard:**
1. **Content zone must truncate** — `min-width: 0` + `flex: 1` + `text-overflow: ellipsis`
2. **Leading/trailing are flex-none** — fixed width, vertically centered
3. **Responsive collapse** — on narrow screens, trailing content may wrap below or metadata stacks
4. **Dividers** — between items, not around them
5. **Interactive rows** — entire row clickable without nesting `<a>` in `<a>` issues
6. **Density** — compact vs comfortable padding without breaking alignment

**What AI gets wrong:**
- Hardcodes widths instead of using flex
- Forgets `min-width: 0` so text pushes layout
- No truncation on names/descriptions
- Trailing content wraps incorrectly
- Avatar sizing doesn't match text rhythm
- No divider pattern (uses borders on items instead of gap/divide)

---

## Recommendations for Move

### 1. Components to build

**`List`** — compound component with these sub-components:

| Sub-component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `List` / `List.Root` | Container: `<ul>` with dividers, size, padding, density |
| `List.Item` | Row: three-zone flex layout (leading / content / trailing) |
| `List.Leading` | Fixed-width leading slot (avatar, icon, checkbox) |
| `List.Content` | Flex-1 content zone with truncation built-in |
| `List.Title` | Primary text line (semibold, truncate by default) |
| `List.Description` | Secondary text line (muted, truncate by default) |
| `List.Trailing` | Fixed-width trailing slot (badge, button, timestamp, menu) |

Optional convenience (inspired by Ant Design's Meta):
| `List.Meta` | Shorthand: `avatar` + `title` + `description` → auto-renders Leading + Content + Title + Description |

### 2. Props consensus

**Root props** (appear in 3+ libraries):
| Prop | Type | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| size | 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' | Controls padding, font size, avatar size, gap |
| dividers | boolean | Show dividers between items (default true) |
| density | 'compact' \| 'default' \| 'comfortable' | Vertical padding scale |
| hover | boolean | Enable hover highlight on items |

**Item props:**
| Prop | Type | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| as | 'li' \| 'a' \| 'button' \| component | Polymorphic — clickable rows render as `<a>` or `<button>` |
| href | string | Shorthand for `as="a" href={...}` |
| onClick | function | Makes row interactive |
| active | boolean | Visual active/selected state |
| disabled | boolean | Dims and prevents interaction |

**Meta props (convenience):**
| Prop | Type | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| avatar | ReactNode | Leading visual |
| title | ReactNode | Primary text |
| description | ReactNode | Secondary text |

### 3. Composition: Compound

Strongly compound. The three-zone layout is the whole point — each zone needs independent control.

**API should support both composition and shorthand:**

```tsx
{/* Full composition — maximum control */}
<List>
  <List.Item href="/users/1">
    <List.Leading><Avatar src="..." size="md" /></List.Leading>
    <List.Content>
      <List.Title>Jane Cooper</List.Title>
      <List.Description>jane@example.com</List.Description>
    </List.Content>
    <List.Trailing>
      <Badge color="green">Active</Badge>
    </List.Trailing>
  </List.Item>
</List>

{/* Meta shorthand — covers 80% of cases */}
<List>
  <List.Item>
    <List.Meta
      avatar={<Avatar src="..." />}
      title="Jane Cooper"
      description="jane@example.com"
    />
    <List.Trailing>
      <Badge color="green">Active</Badge>
    </List.Trailing>
  </List.Item>
</List>
```

### 4. Animation

- **Enter stagger** — same as Timeline: items fade+slideUp with stagger delay (80ms)
- **Hover** — subtle background color transition (CSS, not JS animation)
- **Active state** — subtle left border or background accent (CSS transition)
- No exit animations needed (lists are typically persistent)

### 5. Component class

**Data display** — lives in `src/components/data/List/`, same category as Timeline and Table.

### 6. Default candidates (not decisions)

| Default | Value | Confidence |
|---------|-------|------------|
| size | 'md' | High |
| dividers | true | High |
| density | 'default' | High |
| hover | false | Medium — depends on whether items are typically interactive |
| Item `as` | 'li' | High |
| truncation (Title) | true (single-line ellipsis) | High |
| truncation (Description) | true (single-line ellipsis) | Medium — some cases need 2 lines |

### 7. Key decisions (resolved)

1. **Meta sub-component** — YES, included as optional convenience. Saves 4 sub-components per item for the 80% case.
2. **Sticky section headers** — DEFERRED to v2. `List.Group` with sticky label is niche.
3. **Interactive rows** — Polymorphic `as` prop on Item (`'li' | 'a' | 'button'`). Simpler than MUI's separate ListItemButton.
4. **Loading/pagination** — SKIP. Consumer responsibility, not List's job.
5. **Grid mode** — SKIP. Use Grid component instead.
6. **Description line clamping** — YES. `lines` prop on Description (`1 | 2 | 3 | 'none'`, default `1`).
7. **Responsive collapse** — YES. Container query on Item for trailing content wrap. Solves the #1 AI responsiveness failure.
